title: Rational projective weight coordinates
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $T$ a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], $E$ a vector space with finite basis $b=(b_i)_{i\in I}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and $\rho:T\to\mathrm{GL}_I$ a rational representation [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Characters and cocharacters, and the Laurent-coordinate value of a $\mathbf G_m$-point, are those of [def-sfb-rank-one-root-interfaces], using the multiplicative group [def-sc-gm-ga]. On projective space of lines $P=\mathbf P(I;\operatorname{Spec}k)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], define the following coordinate interfaces. For a commutative $k$-algebra $A$, the vector $v\in A^I$ represents $y\in P(A)$ if its entries, viewed as sections of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, generate the unit ideal and the coordinate morphism $[v_i]$ is $y$. The vector action is the matrix $\rho_A(t)$ times $v$. An algebraic action on $P$ is induced by $\rho$ if for every $A,t,v,y$, a vector representing $y$ is sent by that matrix to a vector representing $ty$; local trivializations make this a condition on all projective points. A vector $e\in E$ has character $\chi$ if $\rho_A(t)(b(e)\otimes1)=\chi_A(t)(b(e)\otimes1)$ for every $A,t$. A cocharacter $\ell$ separates a finite character family $(\chi_c)$ with integer pairings $(m_c)$ if the $m_c$ are pairwise distinct and $\chi_c\ell$ pulls back the Laurent coordinate to $t^{m_c}$ over every algebra. Finally, for $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_k(E,k)$, define $D(f)$ to be the generating locus [def-sc-section-generating-locus] of the section $\sum_i f(b_i)z_i$ of the recorded twisting line $\mathcal O_P(1)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], where the coefficients are pulled back along $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.
